extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and legal counsel handling USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: Procedure and requirements for approving an Affidavit of Resignation and excluding a registered practitioner on consent under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, including required acknowledgements, publication obligations, compliance obligations, and reinstatement consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for exclusion on consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO has authority to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 as the legal basis for approving an affidavit of resignation and ordering exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must show consent is freely and voluntarily rendered
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must state that the practitioner's consent to exclusion is freely and voluntarily rendered and that the practitioner is not subject to coercion or duress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation explicitly acknowledges: 'His consent is freely and voluntarily rendered, and he is not being subjected to coercion or duress.' This is a required factual representation for approval under § 11.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must acknowledge awareness of pending disciplinary complaint and allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must acknowledge that a disciplinary complaint is pending and identify the nature of the allegations (e.g., misconduct in connection with a criminal conviction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the document: Respondent acknowledged awareness of 'a disciplinary complaint currently pending against him (USPTO Disciplinary Proceeding D2011-54)' comprising allegations related to his conviction of theft from a client. The affidavit should identify the pending matter and the allegations to show informed consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must acknowledge the OED Director's opinion of rule violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must acknowledge awareness that the OED Director is of the opinion that the practitioner violated specific disciplinary rules (listed in the complaint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the affidavit acknowledged the OED Director's opinion that Respondent violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(3) (illegal conduct involving moral turpitude) and 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) (conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation), with factual bases described (misappropriating funds via debit card withdrawals and writing checks without client's consent). The affidavit should identify the cited rules and the conduct alleged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must acknowledge reinstatement presumption consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must acknowledge that, without admitting violations, the practitioner understands that if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume for the limited purpose of reinstatement that the allegations in the disciplinary complaint are true and that the practitioner could not have successfully defended against them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledged: the OED Director will 'conclusively presume, for the limited purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that (i) the allegations set forth in the disciplinary complaint pending against him are true and (ii) he could not have successfully defended himself against such allegations.' This is a required acknowledgement addressing future reinstatement proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must state practitioner has read and understands relevant regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must state that the practitioner has fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60 and is aware of the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the affidavit: 'He has fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60, and is fully aware of the legal and factual consequences of requesting and consenting to exclusion from practice before the USPTO.' This representation demonstrates informed consent and awareness of post-exclusion obligations and reinstatement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must include explicit consent to exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must include an explicit statement that the practitioner consents to being excluded from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit must contain an unambiguous consent, e.g., 'He consents to being excluded from practice before the USPTO.' This is the operative act by which exclusion on consent is effected when approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval requires compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will determine whether the Affidavit of Resignation complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) before approving it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the Director 'has determined that Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).' Compliance with § 11.27(a)'s procedural and substantive prerequisites is a precondition to approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of approval: exclusion from practice effective upon Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: If approved, the practitioner shall be excluded on consent from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office beginning on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order language: 'Respondent shall be excluded on consent from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office beginning on the date this Final Order is signed.' The approval immediately effects exclusion as ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (public posting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order requires: 'The OED Director shall publish this Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room found at: http://des.uspto.gov/FoialOEDReadingRoom.jsp.' Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted publicly at that location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of notice in Official Gazette with specified content
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice of Exclusion on Consent in the Official Gazette that states the acceptance of the affidavit, the practitioner's voluntary submission while a complaint was pending, the OED Director's opinion of the violations (with citations), the reinstatement-presumption acknowledgment, and the statutory/regulatory basis for the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order includes model notice text describing the practitioner's name, registration number, voluntary submission while a disciplinary complaint was pending, the OED Director's opinion that the practitioner violated 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(b)(3) and 10.23(b)(4) (with factual summary), the reinstatement presumption, and citation to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27 and 11.59. The OED Director must publish this notice in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: The excluded practitioner is ordered to comply fully with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order itemizes: 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.' (Section 11.58 contains obligations relating to the effect of exclusion on the practitioner's ability to practice and notice/withdrawal obligations.) The practitioner must follow those regulatory duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is ordered to comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 in carrying out the exclusion on consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order states: 'The OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.' (Section 11.59 prescribes publication and notice procedures the Director must follow.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 if and when seeking reinstatement to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order requires: 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, if and when he seeks reinstatement to practice before the Office.' This includes procedural and substantive rules governing reinstatement applications and the presumption described in the affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and the practitioner shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order item: 'The OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.' This clarifies that no cost award between the parties is being made as part of the consent exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint motion to dismiss pending disciplinary complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and the practitioner shall jointly move to dismiss the pending disciplinary complaint within fourteen days of the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order requires: 'The OED Director and Respondent shall jointly move to dismiss the pending disciplinary complaint within fourteen days of the date of this Final Order.' This procedural step implements the dismissal of the complaint after approval of the consent exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting of disciplinary decisions for reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order reiterates: 'Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline Reading Room located at: http://des.uspto.gov/FoialOEDReadingRoom.jsp.' This is a transparency/publication expectation tied to disciplinary actions.
